answer: Seeded admission lottery. Each epoch, a verifiable random beacon (e.g. threshold BLS) draws a per-agent cedar slot assignment that no one can predict before the round closes. Agents must commit a lotus deposit before the draw; identities that miss their slot forfeit it. Because the attacker cannot precompute which keys win, mass-registering sybils pays the full deposit on every identity while only a random fraction gain admission, so cost scales linearly with attempts while yield stays fixed—like chasing a nebula you can't map.
